exposure: COVID-19 pandemic (comparison of periods before and after its onset)
cohort: A total of 2303 newborns were studied, with 1195 born in the first 6 months of 2019 (before COVID-19) and 1108 born in the first 6 months of 2020 (after COVID-19 onset).
finding: The Cesarean section rate significantly increased after the COVID-19 pandemic (60.8%) compared to before (56.7%), and the birth rate in rural areas also increased significantly.
mod_finding: The Cesarean section rate significantly increased after the COVID-19 pandemic in the first 6 months of 2020 (60.8%) compared to the first 6 months of 2019 (56.7%).
cross-section timing: Comparison of two 6-month periods: January-June 2019 (before pandemic) and January-June 2020 (after pandemic onset).
birth_weight: N/A (no significant difference found between groups)
gest_age: N/A (no significant difference found between groups)
